text:
Henry's total trip is 60 miles. He stopped first after 20 miles, so he traveled 20 miles from the start to the first stop. His second stop was 15 miles before the end of the trip, meaning the distance from the second stop to the end is 15 miles. Therefore, the distance from the start to the second stop is \(60 - 15 = 45\) miles. The distance traveled between the first and second stops is \(45 - 20 = 25\) miles.

Answer: 25
reasoning:
We are given: "Henry made two stops during his 60-mile bike trip. He first stopped after 20 miles. His second stop was 15 miles before the end of the trip. How many miles did he travel between his first and second stops?"

Total trip = 60 miles.
First stop: after 20 miles. So distance from start to first stop = 20 miles.
Second stop: 15 miles before the end of the trip. So distance from second stop to end = 15 miles. Therefore distance from start to second stop = 60 - 15 = 45 miles.
Distance between first stop and second stop = distance from start to second stop - distance from start to first stop = 45 - 20 = 25 miles.
So answer is 25 miles.
